newsitem.title: BRAZIL: COFFEE - Debt news may mean slower Brazil sales.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE - Debt news may mean slower Brazil sales.

text.p: A decision by Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) to extend the deadline for repayment of producer debt should mean producers will hold back from sales in further months, traders and growers said.
The CMN on October 29 approved some 250 million reais ($243 million) in producer debt be extended for 120 days. Much of the the debt had been due by the end of last month, officials said.
"Normally loans are organised for repayment at the end of October as it gives farmers two months or so to sell after the peak harvest time," said a Banco do Brasil technician.

The bank has not yet received official notification about the CMN decision but the extension was expected to be published officially in the government's official gazette at the beginning of next week, he added.
With the debt burden off producers' backs, growers may now be rather more reluctant than of late to sell coffee in the coming months, traders said.
"I think producers are certainly going to be stiffening their prices. They can see with export shipments and local sales, there is good demand for their coffee," one trader said.

Traders have attributed origin selling in recent weeks in the international markets to the looming debt deadline but this should now dry up, said Joaquim Libanio Leite, export director at Guaxupe co-operative in Minas Gerais.
"The Brazilian producer sells depending on his financial needs," Leite said.
Another good reason for growers to slow down is the growing expectation that the 1997/98 coffee crop will fall short of the recent harvest.

Moreover many farmers also do not believe that the 1996/97 crop is around the 27 million 60-bags plus level forecast by the U.S. Department of Agriculture but instead is nearer to 24 million to 25 million bags, Leite added.
Confirmation of expected higher shipments out of Brazil in October may also have given the international market the impression there is abundant supply in Brazil.

According to the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation, shipments based on bills of lading for the month of October totalled 1.56 million bags by October 31, compared with 999,489 bags by the same state the previous month.
The number of certificates of origin issued had reached 2.08 million bags, well up from the 1.32 million seen in September.
Traders still expect total October exports in excess of 1.7 million bags which would be the highest monthly total since September 1993, according to Febec data.

Last month is seen to be a blip however, benefitting from a September delay in the official lifting of a state export tax. November shipments should be significantly lower, especially given the December/March switch in New York, traders said.
On the export market, some interest was noted in the past few days but nothing to compare with previous weeks.
Swedish quality beans were quoted at around a 12 point discount for December shipment while full description 17/18s were around five under.

In the domestic market, Santos brokers Escritorio Carvalhaes on November 1 quoted fine-to-extrafine Mogiana/Minas green beans at 119/121 reais per 60 kg against the 118/120 reais quoted on October 25.
